The proposed freeway facility constructed within Corridor #5 will be an embankment section for most of its length. All through streets will be bridged to allow for community pedestrian and vehicular traffic circulation. Travel on the local street system will operate more efficiently and safely because much of the airport oriented traffic will be using the freeway.

The results of extensive field noise measurements and predicted 1990 noise levels indicate that some existing levels as well as 1990 levels would exceed the federal noise standards if no abatement is provided. Corrective abatement measures in the form of noise barriers adjacent to both the Airport Spur and I-94 will be provided and all of the resultant noise levels will be reduced to meet the federal noise standards. Hamlin Garland School will also be air conditioned in order to meet the interior noise standards.
The air quality assessment indicates that the air quality impact of the Airport Spur project, after construction, will be minimal. The Airport Spur and development at and around the airport is expected to lead to more intensive use of the area with a significantly heavier total traffic but should not cause significant deterioration of air quality in the area. In spite of projected increases in traffic, the control of vehicle emissions imposed on new vehicles will result in improving air quality conditions within the study area and Milwaukee County whether the project is built or not. The extensive air quality study has been reviewed and approved by the Indirect Source Review Agency.
